content: During pregnancy, glucose metabolism undergoes significant changes. Starting at approximately 16 weeks of gestation, insulin resistance begins to progressively increase. This results in an approximate 5% weekly rise in daily insulin requirements, which continues to escalate and reaches its peak around the 36th week of pregnancy. In the later stages of the third trimester, insulin requirements may decrease. A sudden and rapid decline in insulin needs during this period could be a concerning sign of placental insufficiency and warrants immediate medical evaluation. For individuals with normal pancreatic function, these physiological changes in insulin resistance and requirements are typically well-regulated by the body.
